abstract: We analyze Elman-type recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and their training in the mean-field regime. Specifically, we show convergence of gradient descent training dynamics of the RNN to the corresponding mean-field formulation in the large width limit. We also show that the fixed points of the limiting infinite-width dynamics are globally optimal, under some assumptions on the initialization of the weights. Our results establish optimality for feature-learning with wide RNNs in the mean-field regime.
title: Global optimality of Elman-type RNNs in the mean-field regime

abstract: Discriminative dictionary learning (DL) has been widely studied in various pattern classification problems. Most of the existing DL methods aim to learn a synthesis dictionary to represent the input signal while enforcing the representation coefficients and/or representation residual to be discriminative. However, the $\ell_0$ or $\ell_1$-norm sparsity constraint on the representation coefficients adopted in many DL methods makes the training and testing phases time consuming. We propose a new discriminative DL framework, namely projective dictionary pair learning (DPL), which learns a synthesis dictionary and an analysis dictionary jointly to achieve the goal of signal representation and discrimination. Compared with conventional DL methods, the proposed DPL method can not only greatly reduce the time complexity in the training and testing phases, but also lead to very competitive accuracies in a variety of visual classification tasks.

summary.idea: Projective dictionary pair learning jointly trains two dictionaries: one projects inputs into a representation, and the other reconstructs them. The pair is trained to preserve useful signal information and separate classes.
summary.limitations: No numerical runtime or accuracy comparisons are included in the abstract. It also does not identify the tested tasks, so the size and breadth of the practical advantage remain unclear.
summary.problem: Dictionary-based classifiers represent an input through learned components, but enforcing sparse representations can make both training and prediction expensive. This limits otherwise useful visual recognition methods.
summary.results: The abstract reports greatly reduced training and testing complexity alongside competitive accuracy across several visual classification tasks.
summary.tldr: Learn a direct projection and a reconstruction dictionary together to make dictionary-based classification faster.

title: Projective dictionary pair learning for pattern classification

abstract: We present a novel and unified deep learning framework which is capable of learning domain-invariant representation from data across multiple domains. Realized by adversarial training with additional ability to exploit domain-specific information, the proposed network is able to perform continuous cross-domain image translation and manipulation, and produces desirable output images accordingly. In addition, the resulting feature representation exhibits superior performance of unsupervised domain adaptation, which also verifies the effectiveness of the proposed model in learning disentangled features for describing cross-domain data.
title: A Unified Feature Disentangler for Multi-Domain Image Translation and Manipulation
